pathway.title: Moog Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Revenue is durable over the next twelve months because the order book is large and sales are spread across four segments. The twelve-month backlog of USD 3,250 million, up 23%, equals 75.27% of last-twelve-months net sales, and the largest segment, Space and Defense, was 28.83% of fiscal 2025 net sales against 23.00% for the smallest, Military Aircraft, so near-term sales do not depend on new orders, although customers can reschedule or terminate backlog. Basis: calculation C58; calculation C59; calculation C60; calculation C61; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, page 16

- Growth is cyclical, and the commercial aircraft rebound is its least secure part. Commercial Aircraft sales rose 35.74% from fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2025 and 17.91% in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 on Boeing and Airbus build rates, while Industrial sales fell 3.59% in fiscal 2025 before growing 13.70%, so a rate pause would hit the segment with the largest two-year gain first and government-funded segments would only partly offset it. Basis: calculation C62; calculation C63; calculation C64; calculation C65; 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, page 15

- Customer and contract terms concentrate the risk in government funding and fixed-price work. U.S. Government contracts were 37.85% of fiscal 2025 net sales and Boeing 10.28%, and fixed-price contracts were 90% of over-time sales on the cost-to-cost method, so a funding cut or a cost overrun lands on Moog's margin and cash flow directly. Basis: calculation C68; calculation C69; calculation C71; 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, page 20

- Margins are steady underneath, but the reported margin overstates the run-rate. Gross margin stayed between 27.07% and 28.05% across fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2025 and was 31.10% in the third quarter of 2026, but 28.41% without the tariff recovery against 27.52% a year earlier. Last-twelve-months EBITDA margin was 14.37% as reported and 13.68% without the recovery, which supplied 0.69 percentage points. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C08; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 28

- Operating leverage runs in both directions, so the earnings that lowered leverage could reverse quickly. EBITDA without the recovery grew 29.48% in the third quarter on 15.16% sales growth, which is 1.94 times the pace of sales, while selling, general and administrative cost fell to 13.52% of sales from 14.41%, which the company attributes to higher volume. Basis: calculation C22; calculation C21; calculation C23; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 29

- Free cash flow is improving but not yet proven. Conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow was 10.61% in fiscal 2024, 26.28% in fiscal 2025 and 56.44% over the last twelve months, but customer advances supplied 71.14% of free cash flow in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, and 70.43% of the opening advance balance was recognised as revenue within those nine months, so the float turns over quickly and depends on new advances each period. The fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 delivered more than the whole year's free cash flow, so cash generation also depends on a strong final quarter. Without the advance inflow, nine-month free cash flow was USD 43.65 million. Basis: calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C31; calculation C43; calculation C30; calculation C32; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 32

- Leverage is low on reported debt and moderate on all claims. Counting finance leases lifts net debt to EBITDA to 1.63x and adding receivables sold lifts it to 1.83x, and finance lease liabilities rose over the nine months by about as much as reported debt fell, so total claims were little changed and the fall in leverage came from earnings, not repayment. Cover was 6.88x on cash interest in fiscal 2025 and 9.26x on income-statement interest over the last twelve months, so debt service is comfortable on today's earnings and the exposure is to a fall in EBITDA, not to the interest bill. Basis: calculation C38; calculation C39; calculation C46; calculation C47; calculation C48; calculation C50; calculation C51; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 15

- Refinancing risk is low until 2028 and manageable afterwards. Debt at June 27, 2026 was a USD 164 million drawing on a USD 1,100 million revolving loan and a USD 250 million term loan, both secured by substantially all U.S. assets, USD 500 million of 5.50% senior notes that are unsecured and guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, and USD 5 million on the employee-trust revolver; the legal rank of the secured facilities against the notes is not stated. The bank facilities run to February 2031 and the notes to October 2034, no facility matures within twelve months apart from small term loan installments, and unused capacity was USD 952 million; replacing the 4.25% notes added 125 bp of coupon, which is USD 6.25 million a year, and 45.59% of principal floats, so each 100 bp rise costs USD 4.19 million a year. The nearest funding events are the USD 125 million receivables facility on February 20, 2028 and the employee-trust revolver in April 2028. Basis: calculation C89; calculation C54; calculation C57; calculation C52; calculation C53; calculation C55; calculation C56; calculation C94; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 34

- Covenant compliance is reported but headroom is not established. The loan agreement sets a minimum interest coverage of 3.0x and a maximum net debt to EBITDA of 4.0x on four-quarter figures, with no step-down stated, and the company reports compliance at June 27, 2026 without giving the ratios; covenant EBITDA adds non-cash and synergy items, so it differs from the calculated EBITDA used here, and the agreement also permits up to USD 400 million of incremental facilities, so debt could be added without refinancing the existing ones. Basis: calculation C90; calculation C91; calculation C92; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 34

- Financial policy is the second weak point after disclosure. Shareholder returns were 1.57x free cash flow in fiscal 2024 and 1.40x in fiscal 2025 and were funded by borrowing, then fell to 0.60x in the first nine months of fiscal 2026; trustees of company-funded trusts vote 29.47% of the Class B shares that elect most of the board and no sponsor owns Moog, so creditor protection rests on management restraint that has varied. Basis: calculation C73; calculation C74; calculation C75; calculation C76; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Disclosure quality limits confidence in every ratio. The 2025 annual report revised fiscal 2023, fiscal 2024 and interim results, the auditor gave an adverse opinion on internal control, and the June 2026 quarterly report says the weakness is not remediated; revenue recognised over time, 64.28% of fiscal 2025 sales, rests on cost-to-complete estimates, so the restated trend could move again. Basis: calculation C70; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, pages 105–106; 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 40

runs.text: Five strengths support the credit, in order of weight. First, unused capacity of USD 952 million and no sizeable bank or bond maturity before 2031 mean a slowdown cannot force a refinancing, which is the main protection of the debt. Second, the twelve-month backlog of USD 3,250 million equals 75.27% of last-twelve-months net sales, which protects the next year of revenue and operating cash flow. Third, no segment exceeds 28.83% of net sales, government revenue follows appropriations and aftermarket revenue follows fleet usage rather than new-aircraft build rates, so the book is not tied to a single build rate. Fourth, net debt to EBITDA of 1.36x and cash interest cover of 6.88x leave room for an earnings fall before debt service is stressed. Fifth, gross margin without the recovery rose to 28.41% from 27.52%, which shows the margin gain is not only a one-off. Basis: calculation C57; calculation C58; calculation C60; calculation C35; calculation C50; calculation C10; calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 34

Five weaknesses constrain it, in order of weight. First, free cash flow depends on customer advances and the final quarter: advances supplied 71.14% of nine-month free cash flow and equal 53.59% of total debt, so a reversal would raise net debt by the amount of the float. Second, an adverse opinion on internal control, restated history and cost-to-complete accounting on 64.28% of sales mean every ratio carries estimation risk. Third, customer concentration and fixed-price terms, with the U.S. Government at 37.85% and Boeing at 10.28% of sales, fixed-price terms on 90% of over-time cost-to-cost sales and EBITDA growth of 1.94 times sales growth, mean a funding cut, build-rate cut or overrun would cut earnings by more than sales. Fourth, shareholder returns of 1.57x and 1.40x free cash flow in fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025 under trust-influenced dual-class control show that distributions can outrun cash flow. Fifth, finance leases and receivables sold lift leverage to 1.83x, and total claims including finance leases were little changed over nine months, so the fall in reported leverage came from earnings, not repayment. Basis: calculation C31; calculation C44; calculation C70; calculation C68; calculation C69; calculation C71; calculation C23; calculation C73; calculation C74; calculation C39; calculation C48; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: No sponsor transaction, buyout or recapitalisation is described in the supplied documents; the transactions that matter to creditors are the financing events of fiscal 2025 and 2026 and one small acquisition. On February 26, 2026 Moog entered into an eighth amended and restated loan agreement that extended the revolving loan from 2027 to 2031 and kept a term loan maturing in 2031, with commitments of USD 1,100 million on the revolver. On March 24, 2026 it sold USD 500 million of 5.50% senior notes due October 15, 2034, senior unsecured and guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, and on April 3, 2026 it redeemed all USD 500 million of its 4.25% senior notes due 2027 at par using those proceeds and cash on hand. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34

On January 27, 2026 the receivables purchase agreement was amended to change the administrative agent and extend its maturity to February 20, 2028, with the sale limit unchanged at USD 125 million, and on April 2, 2026 the revolving loan of the employee trust was extended to April 24, 2028. A supplemental indenture dated May 20, 2026 with Truist Bank as trustee was filed as an exhibit; the text does not describe its purpose. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 42

The acquisition of COTSWORKS on July 1, 2025 was paid in cash and in Class A shares and is included in Space and Defense; the sales and results are immaterial in 2026. After the quarter end, a dividend of USD 0.30 per share was declared on July 30, 2026, payable on August 25, 2026. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 25

fields.value: Cash flow quality is improving but uneven. Free cash flow, defined as operating cash flow less purchase of property, plant and equipment, was negative in fiscal 2023 and USD 128.355 million in fiscal 2025, and USD 350.228 million over the last twelve months. Working capital absorbed cash in each fiscal year, mainly inventories and unbilled receivables, so conversion of EBITDA to cash leans on customer advances. Contract advances and progress billings, a non-debt funding float, rose from USD 372.988 million at fiscal 2025 year end to USD 486.574 million at June 27, 2026; if that float reverses as deliveries are made, operating cash flow falls by the same amount and net debt rises.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at June 27, 2026 is cash of USD 66.821 million plus about USD 932 million of undrawn revolving capacity after standby letters of credit, with the revolving loan and the term loan both maturing in 2031. At fiscal 2025 year end most cash was held outside the United States, so the undrawn revolver, not cash, is the usable buffer. The 2026 refinancing replaced the 4.25% notes due 2027 with 5.50% notes due 2034 and extended the revolver from 2027 to 2031, which removes the near-term maturity wall that the fiscal 2025 maturity schedule still shows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt-like claims outside the Total Debt figure matter for creditors. Finance lease liabilities, carried inside accrued liabilities and other long-term liabilities, were USD 172.352 million at June 27, 2026 against USD 134.075 million at fiscal 2025 year end, and USD 125 million of receivables sold under the receivables purchase agreement is derecognised. Adding finance leases to net debt gives 1.63x and adding receivables sold as well gives 1.83x. Operating lease liabilities, pension obligations and purchase commitments are further claims that are not in debt.

fields.value: The data carry three quality risks. First, the 2025 annual report revised fiscal 2023, fiscal 2024 and the interim quarters, and management and the auditor state that internal control over financial reporting was not effective; the 2026 quarterly report says the weakness is not yet remediated, so the restated trend could move again. Second, the latest quarter benefits from a USD 30 million recovery of previously paid tariffs recorded as a reduction of cost of sales; excluding it, net leverage on the last twelve months would be 1.42x, shown as an analyst sensitivity and not applied. Third, the issuer reports no EBITDA, so every EBITDA here is calculated and differs from the loan agreement definition that governs the covenants.

fields.value: The 2026 financing events are dated and sized in the statements. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Moog's four-segment aerospace, defense and industrial business gives creditors durable demand and a large order book, but governance risk is medium because dual-class control, trust-held votes and an unremediated reporting-control weakness limit creditor protection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor owns Moog. In fiscal 2025 shareholder returns were 1.40x free cash flow and net debt rose, while the trustees of company-funded trusts vote 29.47% of the Class B shares that elect most of the board.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C26; calculation C34; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business is diversified by segment and weighted to defense, which steadies cash flow for creditors. The largest segment, Space and Defense, was 28.83% of fiscal 2025 net sales and the smallest, Military Aircraft, 23.00%; defense was 52% of 2026 sales, and aftermarket support was 14% of fiscal 2025 sales.

fields.value: - Customer concentration is moderate but real. Boeing was 10.28% of fiscal 2025 net sales, U.S. Government contracts 37.85%, and the five largest customers about 31%, so a Boeing production cut or a defense funding change would reach sales and cash flow directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The order book supports near-term revenue. The twelve-month backlog was USD 3.0 billion at the 2025 year end, up 20%, and USD 3,250 million at June 27, 2026, up 23%, which reduces the chance that margin gains reverse quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control sits in the share structure and the identity of the controlling holders is not established. Class A shares carry one-tenth of a vote and Class B one vote, Class B holders elect the balance of the board after Class A elects at least 25%, and trustees of the stock employee compensation trust and the supplemental retirement trust vote all trust-held shares: 29.47% of Class B shares outside treasury, or 18.67% of all votes on a calculated basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder returns have run ahead of free cash flow, but the pattern reversed in 2026. Dividends plus treasury purchases were 1.40x free cash flow in fiscal 2025 and 1.57x in fiscal 2024, and 0.60x over the first nine months of fiscal 2026; the difference was funded by debt, which raised net debt over fiscal 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C26; calculation C29; calculation C32; 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisition appetite is modest. The only acquisition in the period, COTSWORKS on July 1, 2025, cost 1.59% of fiscal 2025 net sales and was paid in cash and Class A shares, so it did not strain liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disclosure quality is the weakest governance point. The 2025 annual report revised fiscal 2023, fiscal 2024 and interim results, the auditor gave an adverse opinion on internal control while giving an unqualified opinion on the statements, and the latest quarterly report says the weakness is not yet remediated, so reported earnings carry added estimation risk until it is.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 financing actions were neutral to positive for creditors. The 4.25% notes were redeemed at par with the proceeds of the 5.50% notes due 2034 and cash, the revolver maturity moved to 2031, and no premium or extraction is documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium governance view is that no sponsor owns Moog, the chairman and chief executive are different people, the auditor's opinion on the statements is unqualified, leverage is low, and shareholder returns were covered by free cash flow at 0.60x in the first nine months of fiscal 2026. The view would move to low if the control weakness is confirmed remediated, the proxy statement shows an independent board and names the trustees, and distributions stay below free cash flow. It would move to high if returns or acquisitions were again funded by debt while the weakness remains open, or if the trustees' votes were used to change creditor terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C32; 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, page 140; 10-K_2025-09-27_mog-20250927.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; 10-Q_2026-06-27_mog-20260627.htm.jsonl, page 40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, beneficial ownership above five percent and the identity of the trustees are not established; the governance view therefore rests on share structure and disclosed conduct and could move either way once those are known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed loan agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the legal capacity for distributions and acquisitions is not established; the shareholder-behaviour finding describes conduct, not what the documents permit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer and programme detail beyond Boeing and U.S. Government shares is not supplied, so concentration inside the five largest customers is not established; the durability conclusion is limited to those shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The trust vote shares are calculated from reported share tables and assume treasury shares carry no vote; the filings state no voting percentages, so the control finding is an estimate within a few points.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor transaction, buyout or recapitalisation is described in the supplied documents; the transactions that matter to creditors are the financing events of fiscal 2025 and 2026 and one small acquisition. On February 26, 2026 Moog entered into an eighth amended and restated loan agreement that extended the revolving loan from 2027 to 2031 and kept a term loan maturing in 2031, with commitments of USD 1,100 million on the revolver. On March 24, 2026 it sold USD 500 million of 5.50% senior notes due October 15, 2034, senior unsecured and guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, and on April 3, 2026 it redeemed all USD 500 million of its 4.25% senior notes due 2027 at par using those proceeds and cash on hand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On January 27, 2026 the receivables purchase agreement was amended to change the administrative agent and extend its maturity to February 20, 2028, with the sale limit unchanged at USD 125 million, and on April 2, 2026 the revolving loan of the employee trust was extended to April 24, 2028. A supplemental indenture dated May 20, 2026 with Truist Bank as trustee was filed as an exhibit; the text does not describe its purpose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisition of COTSWORKS on July 1, 2025 was paid in cash and in Class A shares and is included in Space and Defense; the sales and results are immaterial in 2026. After the quarter end, a dividend of USD 0.30 per share was declared on July 30, 2026, payable on August 25, 2026.

fields.value: The strongest case against a cautious reading is breadth and trajectory. The view would improve if the control weakness is closed, full-year free cash flow conversion reaches the guided 70% with contract advances holding, and buybacks stay below free cash flow. It would weaken if the twelve-month backlog falls below USD 3,250 million, contract advances reverse while inventories and unbilled receivables keep rising, or distributions again exceed free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Moog designs, manufactures and integrates precision motion and fluid controls for aerospace, defense and industrial customers in four segments, and sells to original equipment manufacturers and end users, with spares, repair and overhaul support at 14% of fiscal 2025 sales. The business model supports debt service because most revenue is recognised over time on long contracts and is partly funded by customer advances, and because the installed base of flight control systems creates aftermarket demand; it weakens liquidity when a customer delays deliveries, because revenue recognition, billing and advance receipts all slip together while costs continue. Moog is a listed company with no sponsor or parent, Class A and Class B shares carry different votes, trustees of company-funded trusts vote 29.47% of the Class B shares, which is 18.67% of all votes on a calculated basis, and acquisitions have been small, with COTSWORKS costing 1.59% of fiscal 2025 net sales. For creditors this means financial policy is set by management and by a board elected through the share structure, with a dividend of USD 0.30 per share declared on July 30, 2026 and buybacks at management's discretion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable over the next twelve months and cyclical beyond that. The twelve-month backlog equals 75.27% of last-twelve-months net sales, roughly nine months of sales, and the quarterly report attributes the 23% rise to higher narrowbody and widebody orders, higher military aircraft orders, orders across the whole Space and Defense portfolio and demand for data center cooling pumps in Industrial. Over the cycle the exposure is concentrated and regulated: U.S. Government contracts were 37.85% of fiscal 2025 sales and can be terminated, Boeing was 10.28%, and the 2025 annual report says Boeing and Airbus build-rate changes move demand for Moog's flight control systems. Pricing power is limited by the same facts: management's strategy is pricing and simplification, but the risk factors say Moog may be unable to raise prices as fast as supplier prices, and a large customer evaluates the cost of its supplier base. For creditors the implication is stable cash flow while backlog converts and a sharp, correlated fall if build rates or defense funding turn, because the commercial and government exposures do not offset each other in a build-rate pause.

fields.value: Margins can be defended against moderate volume pressure but their resilience in a downturn is unproven, because fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2026 was an upcycle. Fixed-price contracts, 90% of over-time cost-to-cost sales, leave cost overruns with Moog, supplier price inflation and tariffs on steel and aluminum press margins, and Moog says it may be unable to pass them on. In fiscal 2025 gross margin fell 0.66 percentage points while EBITDA margin rose 0.68 percentage points, because research and development fell from 3.12% to 2.43% of sales and impairment, restructuring and other charges fell from 1.73% to 0.65% of sales, not because gross profit improved. In the third quarter of 2026 research and development rose 50.83% for Space and Defense growth programs, which is an investment that lowers cash flow before it lifts sales, and selling, general and administrative cost fell as a share of sales on higher volume, as the company states. For creditors the margin is a support while volume grows and an amplifier on the way down.

fields.value: EBITDA translates into free cash flow unevenly and the durable level is not yet established. Capital expenditure fell from 5.35% of net sales in fiscal 2023 to 3.14% over the last twelve months, which lifted free cash flow but leaves less room to cut further, and management called third-quarter capital expenditure light because of timing, so some of it may return. The nine-month cash flow improved on higher earnings and customer advances on Commercial Aircraft, Space and Defense and Military Aircraft programs, and on lower inventory outflow because Commercial Aircraft material receipts were delayed, which can reverse when supply normalises. Finance lease payments and a pension contribution of USD 10 million expected in 2026 are further fixed calls on cash, and free cash flow is back-end loaded: the first nine months of fiscal 2025 used cash and the fourth quarter delivered the full-year result. For creditors, free cash flow is enough to fund the dividend and modest buybacks in a good year but not a reliable source of deleveraging until advances and inventory normalise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is considerable, with tier one and tier two suppliers and vertically integrated primes, and the annual report notes that suppliers have consolidated to secure long-term sole-source positions that may withstand downturns better than Moog; for creditors this limits pricing power and margin recovery in a slowdown. Buyer power is high because Boeing and the U.S. Government are large buyers that review their supplier base and can curtail programs, which caps the margin on the 37.85% of sales in government contracts. Supplier power matters because some inputs are sole-sourced and prices have risen, which pressures margins when fixed-price contracts prevent pass-through. The filings do not describe entry barriers or substitutes, so those two forces are not established. Political and economic factors are the material external drivers: the February 20, 2026 ruling that tariffs under the emergency powers act were invalid produced a USD 30 million recovery of previously paid tariffs, which is a catch-up rather than a run-rate item, further tariffs on steel and aluminum could raise costs, and defense appropriations and aircraft build rates set demand. Technology is a modest upside through data center cooling pumps in Industrial. In credit terms the strengths are liquidity, backlog and segment balance, the weaknesses are advance-dependent cash flow, control quality and fixed-price exposure, the opportunities are data center cooling and Space and Defense capture, and the threats are a build-rate pause, defense funding delay, tariffs and supplier inflation.

fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months management guides fiscal 2026 net sales of USD 4.4 billion, an adjusted operating margin of 14.1% and free cash flow conversion of 70%, all raised in July 2026, and the backlog supports the sales number. Tailwinds are the 23% backlog rise, orders across Space and Defense, narrowbody and widebody orders, data center cooling pumps and the 80/20 simplification program; headwinds are a tariff recovery of USD 30 million that is a catch-up rather than a run-rate item, a coupon increase of 125 bp on USD 500 million of notes, growth that slows to about 7.82% in the fourth quarter on the guidance, and the delayed material receipts that may return as inventory outflow. Over three to five years the outlook depends on build rates, defense budgets and whether the control weakness is closed; management gives no medium-term forecast, so that horizon is a judgement. For creditors the outlook supports continued deleveraging while volumes grow and little margin for a shock that arrives alongside distributions.

fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins with a Boeing production pause or a defense appropriation delay, which the annual report names as risks, and the first operational break is Commercial Aircraft and Military Aircraft deliveries slipping while Moog keeps building. Because 90% of over-time sales are fixed-price, a slip raises cost to complete and cuts margin, and because EBITDA moved 1.94 times as fast as sales in the third quarter, earnings would fall by more than sales. Cash flow then falls twice: customer advances stop growing and begin to unwind, and because 70.43% of the opening balance was recognised as revenue within nine months the float would run down within roughly a year, while inventories and unbilled receivables build and dividends and buybacks continue. If only the nine-month advance inflow reversed and EBITDA stayed unchanged, net debt to EBITDA would be 1.53x, or 1.61x without the tariff recovery, and even a full reversal of the advance balance would take it to 2.14x, the level of fiscal 2023, so the effect on leverage is a return to earlier levels, not a break. Liquidity absorbs it, because unused capacity of USD 952 million exceeds the whole advance balance and no maturity falls before 2028; management can cut buybacks, hold capital expenditure at 3.14% of sales or lower and slow the dividend. Resilience therefore looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in this scenario, and default risk is not supported by the evidence. The observable triggers are contract advances falling, revolving loan drawings rising above USD 164 million and backlog falling below USD 3,250 million.

fields.value: Overall, Moog presents an adequate business profile supported by a USD 3,250 million twelve-month backlog, balanced segments, low reported leverage and long-dated maturities, but credit quality is constrained by free cash flow that leans on customer advances, an unremediated control weakness and shareholder returns that have exceeded free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but unproven, because conversion rose to 26.28% in fiscal 2025 and 56.44% over the last twelve months while customer advances supplied 71.14% of nine-month free cash flow. Compared with typical leveraged-credit issuers, leverage, liquidity and maturities look stronger and disclosure quality weaker, a judgement because no peer data is supplied. The financial profile is improving, with net debt to EBITDA at 1.36x against 2.14x at fiscal 2023 year end. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued bond market access, as shown in March 2026, and on renewal of the USD 125 million receivables facility before February 20, 2028. Further analysis would require the executed loan agreement and compliance certificate, the proxy statement, the advance schedule by program and the tariff recovery split by segment. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: a Boeing or defense-funding delay that unwinds customer advances while distributions continue.

fields.value: Five strengths support the credit, in order of weight. First, unused capacity of USD 952 million and no sizeable bank or bond maturity before 2031 mean a slowdown cannot force a refinancing, which is the main protection of the debt. Second, the twelve-month backlog of USD 3,250 million equals 75.27% of last-twelve-months net sales, which protects the next year of revenue and operating cash flow. Third, no segment exceeds 28.83% of net sales, government revenue follows appropriations and aftermarket revenue follows fleet usage rather than new-aircraft build rates, so the book is not tied to a single build rate. Fourth, net debt to EBITDA of 1.36x and cash interest cover of 6.88x leave room for an earnings fall before debt service is stressed. Fifth, gross margin without the recovery rose to 28.41% from 27.52%, which shows the margin gain is not only a one-off.

fields.value: Five weaknesses constrain it, in order of weight. First, free cash flow depends on customer advances and the final quarter: advances supplied 71.14% of nine-month free cash flow and equal 53.59% of total debt, so a reversal would raise net debt by the amount of the float. Second, an adverse opinion on internal control, restated history and cost-to-complete accounting on 64.28% of sales mean every ratio carries estimation risk. Third, customer concentration and fixed-price terms, with the U.S. Government at 37.85% and Boeing at 10.28% of sales, fixed-price terms on 90% of over-time cost-to-cost sales and EBITDA growth of 1.94 times sales growth, mean a funding cut, build-rate cut or overrun would cut earnings by more than sales. Fourth, shareholder returns of 1.57x and 1.40x free cash flow in fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025 under trust-influenced dual-class control show that distributions can outrun cash flow. Fifth, finance leases and receivables sold lift leverage to 1.83x, and total claims including finance leases were little changed over nine months, so the fall in reported leverage came from earnings, not repayment.
